noticias.titulo: Visegrád Four leaders voice concerns over EU budget proposal
noticias.resumen: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations.
noticias.texto:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations.
The prime ministers of the Visegrád Four (V4) countries voiced concerns over the European Union's next seven-year budget proposal at a meeting in Bratislava on Monday, questioning spending priorities and plans to include funding for Ukraine.
The leaders were meeting with the Austrian chancellor in Slovakia to discuss economic cooperation, migration and the draft of the budget.
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said his government did not consider the proposal an acceptable starting point for negotiations.
He said he had therefore written to European Council President António Costa to explain that he saw little point in holding a special council meeting scheduled for later in the week as "there is no point spending two days in Brussels not agreeing on anything."
Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš also signalled his concerns over the proposed budget, saying he had expected the European Commission to show at least some sign that it wanted to save money.
He argued that maintaining a European Parliament in three locations was unnecessary and costly, while also voicing concerns over member state contributions.
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, who hosted the meeting, said the leaders had not adopted a joint position on the budget during Monday's meeting, as this had not been the purpose of their discussions, although he noted that they were broadly aligned on the subject.
Funding for Ukraine
For his part, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk spoke mainly about security, saying that Poland was committed to peace but that recent events showed the impact of Russia's invasion of Ukraine on Poland.
Tusk underlined the importance of continuing support for Kyiv, arguing that the country's ability to defend itself was of strategic significance for Europe's security.
However, his Hungarian counterpart, Magyar, warned that "support for Ukraine should not be included in the EU budget."
Magyar said there was no question that Ukraine deserved solidarity and noted that Hungary was already providing various forms of assistance to the Ukrainian people and government.
But he argued that financial support for Ukraine should not be incorporated into the bloc's budget in a way that would make contributions mandatory for all members.
On the same issue, Tusk said he did not think it was a good idea for the EU to finance support for Ukraine through joint borrowing - something the Hungarian government has already made clear that it would not take part in.
At a press conference after the meeting, the leaders stressed that regional cooperation was not only important but also achievable, given their shared positions on a number of key issues.
Fico said the V4 countries and Austria broadly agreed on key issues affecting the region, including cohesion policy, migration policy and agricultural strategies.
One of the main topics was how to deal with illegal migration. All the leaders called for strict rules and their consistent enforcement, while Fico also praised a plan for some EU member states to establish immigration return hubs in Rwanda.
Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said it was in Austria's interest to cooperate with its neighbours and that he wanted the country to be an ally of the V4.
He added that closer cooperation would also help ensure that the rest of the EU better understood developments in central and eastern Europe and the strategic priorities shaping the region.

noticias.titulo: Tanzania: Towering flames engulf beachfront hotels in Zanzibar
noticias.resumen: A massive fire swept through six beachfront hotels on the island of Zanzibar, Tanzania, on Saturday 21 November 2026, forcing around 180 tourists to evacuate as flames spread rapidly along the popular Nungwi Beach.
noticias.texto:
Thick black smoke rolled over the white sands of Nungwi Beach on Zanzibar’s northern tip after an afternoon fire at Makofi Hotel, whipped along by strong winds and thatched roofs, swept into adjacent resorts, restaurants and shops. Eyewitness mobile footage recorded buildings roaring with flames as tourists and locals scrambled down the beach, some hauling suitcases, others pitching in to help, until firefighters drawn from three stations subdued the blaze after approximately three hours. Although several hotel staff sustained injuries, officials confirmed that every one of the 183 tourists escaped unharmed, with more than 20 hotels in Mchangani and Matemwe stepping in to house displaced guests free of charge.
Across the six affected hotels (Makofi, Z Hotel, Nungwi Garden, BR, Pasha and Sand Beach), four restaurants and about 40 shops, the scale of the damage poses an acute challenge for local businesses and workers in the semi-autonomous Tanzanian archipelago, where tourism is an economic mainstay. On Monday, investigators were still working to confirm whether the fire started in a bread-baking oven, as early accounts suggested, while Tourism and Antiquities Minister Nasra Nassor Omar urged patience ahead of an official inquiry and promised a rapid assessment to guide the government’s response.

noticias.titulo: German-Ukrainian interceptor shoots down Russian jet-powered drone, company says
noticias.resumen: The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.
noticias.texto:
The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.
A German-Ukrainian company said on Monday that its SPYS interceptor UAV had shot down a Russian jet-powered drone in Ukraine.
Quantum WIY Industries announced that it had successfully intercepted a Russian Geran-5 K5-K attack drone during combat testing in Ukraine, according to a press release shared by Quantum Systems, a German defence firm that launched the joint venture alongside Ukraine's WIY Drones.
“We need to keep developing and scaling interceptors to protect Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure. Russia keeps adapting its attack systems, so we work closely with Ukrainian brigades to adjust our systems accordingly," Sven Kruck, co-CEO of Quantum Systems, said.
"You can never stand still," he added.
According to WIY Drones, the SPYS system is a high-speed interceptor UAV that can be deployed to defend against aerial targets.
It is designed to counter both attack and reconnaissance drones and to protect military positions, mobile units and critical infrastructure, the company says on its website.
The SPYS interceptor can reach speeds of up to around 450 kph and has a flight ceiling of 4 km, according to WIY.
The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said in early November that Russian forces had begun using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.
The agency said that "based on its aerodynamic scheme and tactical-technical characteristics," the K5-K "can already be classified as a compact cruise missile."
It added that the drone can hit speeds of more than 450 kph and can reach an altitude of 6 km.
Unlike conventional attack drones such as the Geran-2, which use propeller engines, jet-powered drones can hit significantly higher speeds, making them harder for Ukrainian air defences to deal with.

noticias.titulo: Belgium: Workers march against spending cuts as living costs rise
noticias.resumen: Thousands marched through Brussels, on Monday 23 November 2026, against proposed austerity measures, with some clashes prompting police to deploy tear gas and water cannons. The protests came as Belgium's government struggled to agree on its budget for 2027.
noticias.texto:
Carrying placards warning that "Rent is eating into our wages" and "The rich earn more, the workers pay more", demonstrators rallied in Brussels to oppose around €10 billion in proposed spending cuts before clashes broke out with riot police, who responded with tear gas, water cannons and charges as a car burned and officers made arrests amid plumes of smoke. For protesters already squeezed by high energy costs, inflation and shrinking purchasing power, the planned savings threaten to place an unfair burden on the lowest-paid while undermining social security, employment support and help for families.
The street anger spilled over on the very day Prime Minister Bart De Wever met King Philippe to update him on strained talks over Belgium’s 2027 budget. Having set a year-end deadline for coalition partners to sign off on the cuts, and warned that the government could collapse if negotiations fail, De Wever now faces sharpening resistance both inside parliament and on the streets as he seeks to reconcile fiscal discipline with demands to protect living standards.

noticias.resumen: Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer spoke to Chiara Martinelli, the director of Climate Action Network, to look at what went wrong at the COP31 climate talks and what it means for Europe and for the future of global climate action.
noticias.texto:
Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer spoke to Chiara Martinelli, the director of Climate Action Network, to look at what went wrong at the COP31 climate talks and what it means for Europe and for the future of global climate action.
Despite becoming the longest UN climate conference in history over the weekend, the COP31 talks failed to produce a deal after the European Union and a number of countries rejected a final proposal over the omission of fossil fuels.
Across Europe, frustration is growing and questions are being raised about the future of international climate diplomacy. Is the COP process still capable of delivering meaningful results, or has it reached a breaking point?
To explore what went wrong in Turkey, what the failed negotiations mean for Europe and for the future of global climate action, Euronews' Felicia Pochhammer spoke with Chiara Martinelli, the director of Climate Action Network, on Europe Tonight.

noticias.titulo: Merz says it was a 'mistake' not to admit Ukraine into NATO in 2008
noticias.resumen: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters the Russian invasion of Ukraine would likely not have happened if allies had agreed to admit Kyiv in 2008 during a summit in Bucharest.
noticias.texto:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters the Russian invasion of Ukraine would likely not have happened if allies had agreed to admit Kyiv in 2008 during a summit in Bucharest.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz described the decision not to admit Ukraine into NATO in 2008, following a proposal by then-US President George W. Bush, as a “mistake.”
Speaking alongside NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at a press conference in Berlin, Friedrich Merz told reporters: "I think we all see today, at least from the point of view of what a mistake it was, not to follow the American proposal in 2008 at the NATO summit in Bucharest."
He added that the full-scale invasion of Ukraine would have been 'prevented' had the alliance opened up membership back then.
"If Ukraine had become a member of NATO, this war would have been likely to be prevented," said Merz, in comments that were translated from German.
The meeting came amid ongoing US-led negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, with Rutte visiting the German capital for the NATO Parliamentary Assembly's annual meeting.
Rutte struck a cautious tone on the prospect of reviving discussions about Ukraine's NATO membership, stressing that successful peace negotiations would need to come first.
The remarks came in response to recent comments by French President Emmanuel Macron, who called for the debate over Ukraine's membership of the alliance to be reopened.
Kyiv's potential NATO membership has resurfaced as part of a potential final resolution to ending the war.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has reportedly indicated he would be willing to end the war in Ukraine, provided NATO agrees to return to its 1997 posture. This would effectively mean reversing the alliance's subsequent expansion by withdrawing membership from countries that joined after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
However, NATO membership for Ukraine remains a distant prospect, according to Rutte. He noted that while "it's a long-standing position that Ukraine should be a part of NATO," there is no unanimous agreement among alliance members on its accession.
Rutte also rebuffed the notion that the Kremlin could have any say in the current or future makeup of the NATO alliance. "What cannot happen is we are forced to roll back NATO to the 1997 borders," he said.
"It's only the 32 allies deciding who is in NATO and who is not in NATO".
Rutte was also addressing ongoing tensions in Europe over increasing Russian hybrid attacks, including last week's incursion into Poland, when two Russian cruise missiles and a drone landed on Polish territory, according to Polish officials.
He attributed Russia's increased aggression to mounting battlefield casualties, claiming that Russian forces are losing up to 50,000 soldiers each month in Ukraine. He contrasted this figure with Soviet losses in Afghanistan and US casualties during the Vietnam War.
"Ukraine is rolling back the frontline in the direction of Russia and striking deep" into Russian territory, Rutte told journalists.
Rutte reiterated NATO's position that the best solution to growing hybrid attacks is doubling down on support for Ukraine.
"Most importantly, we need to keep our military support for Ukraine going," said Rutte.
"For every incident in Europe - more support for Ukraine," he added.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian President Vladimir Putin had ordered the strikes following what he described as “weak meetings” with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
“Russia is trying to compensate for its military and diplomatic impotence with precisely this kind of terror," Zelenskyy wrote in a post on "X" last Friday.
Separately, NATO ambassadors met in Brussels Monday to discuss the Russian incursion into Poland. The alliance is now considering deploying more assets to the region in response.
NATO's chief military officer, the Supreme Allied Commander (SACEUR) is now "examining the deployment of additional assets as he continues to assess our deterrence and defence posture in Poland and elsewhere," a NATO official confirmed to Euronews.

noticias.titulo: 'Don't waste those talents': GTA VI hacker released on licence
noticias.resumen: Arion Kurtaj managed to obtain 90 gameplay videos from Rockstar's much anticipated and at the time unfinished GTA VI game before leaking them online under the pseudonym "TeaPotUberHacker."
noticias.texto:
Arion Kurtaj managed to obtain 90 gameplay videos from Rockstar's much anticipated and at the time unfinished GTA VI game before leaking them online under the pseudonym "TeaPotUberHacker."
A 21-year-old man was sentenced to seven years in prison in the United Kingdom on Monday after a string of cyberattacks targeting major companies including Grand Theft Auto VI maker Rockstar Games.
Arion Kurtaj, who was released on licence after already having spent years in custody, pleaded guilty last Monday to a series of hacking attacks that he carried out between 2021 and 2022 as part of the Lapsus$ hacking group.
"You are obviously a very talented young man," the judge said.
"Don't waste those talents by spending the rest of your life in and out of prison," he continued, adding that the sentencing decision required "balancing the seriousness of what you did with, on the other hand, your young age" and medical diagnoses.
Prosecutors said Kurtaj had caused "serious disruption to major international business" and put sensitive information at risk with the hacks.
In one incident, Kurtaj managed to obtain 90 gameplay videos from Rockstar's much anticipated and at the time unfinished GTA VI game before leaking them online under the pseudonym "TeaPotUberHacker." He also threatened to release the game’s source code, according to prosecutors.
Kurtaj is said to have used just a mobile phone, a hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and an Amazon Firestick to carry out the hack.
He also targeted neobank Revolut and ride-hailing firm Uber.
Kurtaj was initially arrested in September 2022 but was deemed not fit to stand trial following a medical assessment.
In 2023, he was handed an indefinite restricted hospital order. A court ruled in January 2026 that the hospital order could be lifted, and his case was scheduled for trial.

noticias.titulo: Iran carries out flogging of singer who performed without hijab
noticias.resumen: Ahmadi and four members of her concert team received lashes in Qom on Monday, her lawyer said, over a December 2024 performance, streamed live without an audience. A court sentenced nine team members to 74 lashes each, a two-year travel ban, and a two-year ban on artistic activity.
noticias.texto:
Ahmadi and four members of her concert team received lashes in Qom on Monday, her lawyer said, over a December 2024 performance, streamed live without an audience. A court sentenced nine team members to 74 lashes each, a two-year travel ban, and a two-year ban on artistic activity.
Iran flogged pop singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her concert team on Monday following a December 2024 performance near Qom in which she sang without a hijab, her lawyer said.
Lawyer Mostafa Nili told Emtedad news channel that the Qom prosecutor's office enforcement team carried out the sentence against Ahmadi in the early hours of Monday.
The flogging sentences against band members Sohail Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri and Amirali Pirnia, and concert organiser Mohsen Lashkari, were carried out on the same day, Nili said.
A criminal court in Qom province had sentenced nine members of the concert team to 74 lashes each, a two-year ban on leaving the country and a two-year ban on artistic activity.
The judiciary also sealed off the Deyr Gachin Caravanserai, the historic venue where the concert took place.
'Hypothetical concert'
Ahmadi performed at the caravanserai near the historic city of Qom on the evening of 11 December 2024 without hijab. No audience was present.
The concert was broadcast live on YouTube and drew around 3 million views in the days that followed.
Ahmadi described the performance as a "hypothetical concert." Writing on her YouTube channel, she said, "I want to sing for the people I love. This is a right that I could not give up, that is, singing for the land that I love passionately."
The criminal court of Qom charged the group with "offending public decency by producing and disseminating vulgar and immoral content online."
Amnesty International called in June for the sentences to be quashed, saying flogging was "a cruel, inhuman and degrading punishment" that violated the absolute prohibition on torture and other ill-treatment.
The organisation called on Tehran to abolish compulsory veiling and corporal punishment and to end the criminalisation of freedom of expression.
Tehran regime contradictions
Under Islamic Republic law, women are banned from singing in public in spaces where men are present.
Although criminal law does not explicitly criminalise women's singing as such, female performers typically face charges of encouraging corruption and prostitution, failing to observe hijab, or offending public decency.
Authorities have used the charge in recent years to close many Instagram pages belonging to Iranian female singers. Appearing in public without hijab is punishable by between 10 days and two months in prison, up to 74 lashes or a fine.
The sentences against Ahmadi and her collaborators stand in contrast to scenes from pro-government rallies held during the US and Israeli military strikes on Iran earlier in 2026, when images circulated widely showing women at the gatherings without mandatory hijab.
A performance by Lebanese singer Julia Boutros was also broadcast at a pro-government gathering in Tehran, where Boutros also did not wear hijab.
Earlier, during the Woman, Life, Freedom protest movement in 2022, Ahmadi had performed the protest song "Az khun-e javanan-e vatan" or "From the blood of the nation's youths".
After it was widely shared on social media, her home was searched by security forces and she was ordered to report to the security prosecutor's office in Tehran.
The Woman, Life, Freedom movement emerged in Iran in September 2022 following the death of Mahsa Amini, 21, in the custody of Tehran's morality police. Amini had been detained over alleged issues with her hijab.
Human rights organisations say the subsequent crackdown left more than 500 people dead.

noticias.titulo: No, Greenland isn't being handed over to Trump. But what exactly has Washington secured?
noticias.resumen: The agreement builds on a 1951 defence agreement and comes after months of heightened tensions between Washington and the island under Danish sovereignty.
noticias.texto:
The agreement builds on a 1951 defence agreement and comes after months of heightened tensions between Washington and the island under Danish sovereignty.
A new deal sealed in September and ratified by Denmark last week is boosting Washington's military presence in Greenland, while also giving it the right to block strategic investments by non-NATO and non-EU countries.
At the same time, it also explicitly reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as Greenlanders' right to self-determination.
What does the US get out of this deal?
The US already operates Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland, an important site for missile warning and space surveillance.
But the new agreement lets Washington expand activities there and establish two additional defence areas: Narsarsuaq in the south and Mestersvig in the east.
It's also meant to give US aircraft broad overflight and landing rights across the island and provide access for Washington’s vessels in its territorial waters.
On top of that, it includes the possible deployment of Trump's proposed Golden Dome missile-defence system.
Troop numbers, construction budgets or deployment dates haven't yet been defined.
For Greenland, the agreement brings potential economic benefits, but also tighter security restrictions.
The US commits to awarding contracts for building and maintaining military facilities to Greenlandic companies as far as possible. That could create jobs and business opportunities.
What does the deal mean for the EU?
The EU is not a party to the agreement, and Greenland's status as an Overseas Country and Territory remains unchanged.
But the deal has important strategic and economic implications for Europe.
First, the investment restrictions could help limit Chinese and Russian influence over critical infrastructure and natural resources in the Arctic.
European investors are not excluded by the agreement. The EU already has a raw-materials partnership with Greenland, and the European Commission announced a separate 200-million-euro investment package in September covering areas including connectivity, energy and critical raw materials. But there is a strategic trade-off.
The agreement reinforces a US-centred security framework in the Arctic. And the EU has no formal role in deciding the island's new American military arrangements.
Does the agreement give US ownership over minerals?
The deal also restricts certain foreign investments in sensitive sectors, including critical infrastructure and natural resources.
“Big investments, there shouldn't be a backdrop for China to get into having a part in big mining projects", Rasmus Leander Nielsen, Associate Professor at the University of Greenland, told Euronews.
"But that de facto has been the case for several years already. So it's not something completely new."
Greenland must implement these rules in cooperation with Denmark, whose authorities will consult Washington on investment decisions. The aim is to limit potentially hostile foreign influence, particularly from countries outside the Western alliance.
For Greenland, however, this could narrow the pool of investors available to develop its economy and natural resources.
The agreement does not give the US ownership of Greenland's minerals or ban all non-Western investment. But it gives Washington a more formal role over certain foreign investments on the island.
Cost of living crisis: Is taxing the rich the way to go?
Also in today's episode, we look at growing calls across Europe to tax the wealthiest people more, as protests continue across the continent over the cost of living.
According to Eurobarometer, around two-thirds of Europeans back this approach. However, in most countries, popular support struggles to turn into concrete legislative action. Take Belgium, where fraught budget talks are ongoing to tackle the deficit.
As part of this, the coalition, made up of centre, left and right-wing parties, clashed after two parties demanded the rich help fill the gap.
This left-right divide also caused a political crisis in the Netherlands this month.
In Europe, countries like Switzerland, Norway and Spain already impose annual net wealth taxes. They generate between 0.2% and 1% of GDP, so the value is often difficult to quantify.
Economists warn that these measures can also discourage investments as well as increase the risk of tax avoidance.
"A net worth tax will probably not get you a lot of money and it will cost you growth. That's something that I see as very dangerous in Europe at the moment. In an economic environment that is very weak in general," told Euronews Dr Michael Christl, Research Fellow at Tax Foundation Europe.
What are the alternatives?
Another avenue is focussing on housing wealth. Britain, for example, will add an annual surcharge on homes worth over £2 million from 2028.
VAT reforms are also part of the conversation, but some experts warn that higher VAT hurts lower- and middle-income households most, since they spend a bigger share of their income on consumption.
And under current EU VAT rules, countries cannot introduce a higher VAT rate exclusively for luxury goods.
No single tax ticks every box, so the answer may lie in a mix of smaller reforms.
But as the political crises in Belgium and the Netherlands over this debate show, agreeing on which ones is the hard part.

In just under 11 minutes, our new format goes beyond the headlines to make sense of what's happening, fact-checking and untangling the day's most pressing issues to explain why they matter to you.

noticias.titulo: United Kingdom to host 2035 Women's World Cup, FIFA confirms
noticias.resumen: The chief executives of the English, Northern Irish, Scottish and Welsh football associations released a joint statement on Monday calling it a "landmark moment."
noticias.texto:
The chief executives of the English, Northern Irish, Scottish and Welsh football associations released a joint statement on Monday calling it a "landmark moment."
The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is set to be hosted by England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales, FIFA confirmed on Monday, marking the first time a World Cup will have been held in the UK since the 1966 men's tournament.
The bid - the only one for the tournament - was approved by acclamation during a virtual meeting of the world governing body's member associations on Monday.
The meeting also saw the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica awarded hosting duties for the 2031 edition, which will see 48 teams take part for the first time.
The 2035 "All Together" bid proposed holding fixtures across 19 grounds, including London's Wembley and Emirates stadiums, Windsor Park in Belfast, Hampden Park in Glasgow and Cardiff's Principality Stadium.
The chief executives of the four associations released a joint statement on Monday calling it a "landmark moment for England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales."
"What follows now is eight and a half years of work; on facilities, on coaching, on officiating, on the pathways that take a girl from her first game to a professional contract," they said. "A tournament of this scale is an opportunity for the whole of the women’s game, and we want its benefits felt in the places that need them most."
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said that the 2031 and 2035 women's tournaments "should reach far beyond the pitch."
"More women player(s), more girls inspired, more women coaches, more women referees, more women administrators, more women leaders. Our priorities for the women's game are very, very simple: we have to expand the game globally, we have to close the gaps that still, of course, exist and we have to build the future together," he added.
2027
The next FIFA Women's World Cup is due to kick off in Brazil in June 2027, running from the 24 June to 25 July.
Host cities include Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, with matches set to be held in iconic stadiums such as the Maracanã.

noticias.titulo: Von der Leyen and Kushner clash over peace talks sequence
noticias.resumen: Ursula von der Leyen and Jared Kushner cannot agree on when and how the issue of European security archicture should be discussed in the peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine.
noticias.texto:
Ursula von der Leyen and Jared Kushner cannot agree on when and how the issue of European security archicture should be discussed in the peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine.
A friction point has emerged between the European Union and the United States over the sequence in the peace talks to end Russia's war on Ukraine, particularly when and how the question of European security architecture should be addressed.
European leaders see the topic as a Russian trap and insist a ceasefire in Ukraine must come first. But in a social media post, US special envoy Jared Kushner, who is brokering the negotiations, said it should be tackled head-on, without waiting.
"Security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalised in isolation from post-war European security architecture. The two must be considered together," Kushner wrote.
Among these potential guarantees, he said, is a provision fashioned after NATO's Article 5 of collective defence to aid Ukraine in the event of a new Russian attack.
US President Donald Trump would sign off on an Article 5-like clause only if "the broader security arrangements made it highly unlikely that the guarantee would ever be invoked", Kushner warned.
This, he argued, makes it necessary for the matter to be on the table from the get-go as part of a bigger deal.
"Nothing is agreed until it is agreed," he said.
Kushner's assertion clashed with the position of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and other European leaders.
They all agree that it is up to Russia to restore the security architecture that European nations established after World War II in multiple treaties and conventions and that Moscow broke when it invaded Ukraine.
Von der Leyen says discussions on security architecture are contingent on Russia establishing a ceasefire in Ukraine and demonstrating a genuine commitment to peace.
Asked about Kushner's latest post, the Commission held its ground.
"Our position has not changed since last week," Paula Pinho, the Commission's chief spokesperson, said in reply to a Euronews question.
"So once there is a ceasefire, then discussions can take place on Europe's security architecture. Those discussions need to take place in the appropriate forum, meaning with NATO allies and with the EU member states fully involved," she added.
"So we stick to our position."
Chancellor Friedrich Merz echoed von der Leyen's view last Thursday while hosting allies, including Kushner, for a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin.
The meeting saw a strong pushback against any attempts to divide the continent into spheres of influence.
"What's needed now is the right sequence, the right order: first peace in Ukraine, then agreements on Euro-Atlantic security," Merz said in the closing press conference.
"Moscow knows: Its maximalist demands from December 2021 are unrealistic."
These demands resurfaced in a paper tabled by Russia at the last round of talks in Abu Dhabi. According to the New York Times, the wish list asks NATO to stop its expansion, withdraw its troops to 1997 borders and halt military support for Ukraine.
Europeans have rejected the requests outright, saying they are a ploy to divert attention from Ukraine and gain veto powers to which Russia is not entitled.
"What cannot happen is that we are forced to roll back NATO to the 1997 borders or that we should have others to decide our posture other than allies themselves," NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said on Monday.
But the prominence that both Moscow and Washington have attached to the security architecture makes it increasingly difficult for Europeans to ignore. Privately, officials admit the subject will have to be discussed one way or another.
The real test will happen when and if Russia agrees to hold multilateral talks with the US, Ukraine and Europe at the same time, something it has so far refused to do.
In his post, Kushner said the US intended to reach a "common understanding" on security architecture "over the coming weeks".
