In an interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump said he had contacted board members because he considered Nvidia strategically important to the United States.
"I'I found the board to be very, very reasonable," Trump said.
Nvidia announced on Monday that its board had unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as president and CEO, effective immediately.
The decision came after the board initially said it did not intend to bring him back, despite Huang expressing his willingness to return.

noticias.titulo: COP must change after Antalya failure, UK climate chief warns
noticias.resumen: Rachel Kyte said it was time to “blow the whistle” on COP’s failings.
noticias.texto: LONDON — The U.N. climate COP process needs urgent reform before next year’s summit in Ethiopia, the U.K.’s top climate official said. Rachel Kyte said countries must “take a red pen” to COP bureaucracy in order to save the talks. COP31 talks in Antalya, Turkey, broke down without a deal on Sunday — the first time in 17 years that countries have failed to reach consensus. The U.K., alongside the EU, many developing countries and small island states, rejected a draft deal that omitted any reference to fossil fuels, which fuel global warming. Kyte, the U.K.’s special representative for climate change and one of London’s key negotiators at COP, told POLITICO that, with reform, the collapse of a deal in Turkey could yet prove a “cathartic moment” for the climate talks. She also said many countries “want to look at” the way COP agreements are made. Final COP texts must currently be agreed by consensus among nearly 200 countries. EU climate chief Wopke Hoekstra also told the Financial Times this week that the U.N. “needs to look into” this approach. Kyte said it had been “a difficult political decision” to reject the deal. “But really I think it was the right year to say ‘no text.’” Catharsis For the COP process to get back on track, reform is needed before next year’s conference, Kyte said. COP32 is scheduled to start in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, in November 2027. “If we can be our best selves, self-organized, over the next 12 months, we will look back on COP31 as being a cathartic moment of reckoning,” she said. “I’m getting incoming calls from all kinds of places, saying: ‘This is a moment, we have to seize it.’ So, on balance, it was a tough call [to reject the deal], but I think it was the right one.” Kyte also called for changes to the “extraordinarily powerful and dominant” role given in recent years to the COP host — the presidency — which she said too often “asserts its agenda” on talks. This year’s co-hosts, Turkey and Australia, placed a major emphasis on a new electrification target, against the wishes of many countries. Kyte said that, if the U.K. and other countries had compromised on the draft deal, it might have left Ethiopia with a “messy set of agreements” to start from. “Better for them that it’s now that we say, ‘Look, this process isn’t working,’” she said. Participants are seen at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey on Nov. 9, 2026. | Burak Kara/Getty Images COPs need to become leaner and more focused on core priorities of climate mitigation and finance for poorer countries to decarbonize and adapt to a warming planet, she added. Next year Summits now had a “ridiculous agenda” of items to tackle, she said, while talks could also be sidetracked by pet projects pursued by COP hosts. “The presidency cannot, or should not, assert its agenda substantively onto the COP, and I had some very interesting conversations with China and a number of other countries [saying]: ‘We need to look at this.’” Kyte added: “That is not unsurprising in a multilateral bureaucratic process that we would have got ourselves into this place — but now’s the time to blow the whistle, right?” She criticized a “proliferation of of procedural issues, which don’t necessarily help move the agenda forward.” Next year’s COP will come one year before the planned conclusion of the second ‘global stocktake,’ a major milestone at which countries review progress on climate goals. U.N. scientists already say the world will overshoot the most ambitious 1.5 degrees celsius warming goal set out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. “The stocktake is, unless a miracle happens, going to show that we’re not on track,” Kyte said. She said COP needed to get back on track to ensure countries could be “more urgent” in their response to its findings, particularly in supporting poorer states. She insisted, though, that, regardless of what happens at COP, market forces were now working in favor of decarbonization, with accelerated uptake of electric vehicles and renewable energy. “I think that the trend of investment in some aspects — battery storage and renewables — [is] already underway,” she said. “And that’s unstoppable at this point.”

noticias.titulo: Bulgaria faces EU fine over runaway public finances
noticias.resumen: The potential penalty emerged during Brussels’ latest round of economic oversight.
noticias.texto: BRUSSELS — The European Commission on Tuesday threatened to slap a fine worth up to €23 million on Bulgaria for failing to rein in spending. Hungary also faces Brussels’ wrath over its public finances. But Budapest’s punishment would be limited to frozen EU funds, as fines of up to 0.02% of GDP are reserved for countries within the single currency union. Bulgaria could suffer both, although the size of the fine still needs to be decided. “We expect the decision to be taken on the fine late this year or very early next year,” Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis told reporters. Both countries could be cut off from some EU funds unless they comply with Brussels’ fiscal demands by spring. The threats emerged during Brussels’ latest round of economic oversight, known as the European Semester, which tries to keep public finances in check amid runaway spending and rising debt across the bloc. The looming fine against Bulgaria is particularly symbolic, as the country only joined the eurozone in January . The fine will be the first to be imposed for breaching the EU’s fiscal rules, which aim to keep the gap between government spending and revenue below 3% of economic output. They also try to limit public debt-to-GDP ratios to below 60%. Bulgaria’s debt pile is well below the EU’s 60% threshold. But its budget deficit is forecast to reach 5% of GDP this year, and Brussels believes Sofia hasn’t done enough to tackle it. The closest Brussels came to administering fines under its fiscal rules was 10 years ago against Spain and Portugal. Ultimately, it reduced the fines to €0 . The EU reformed the rules after the pandemic to address the bloc’s growing debt after governments spent their way out of the deepest recession since World War II. Under the new regime, the fines are smaller so that Brussels can administer them without undermining countries’ finances. “The idea was that the massive fines would make it too unattractive to violate the rules,” Dombrovskis said. But the massive fines also made it “too unattractive to implement the rules.” “That’s why we made the [fines] much, much smaller” and “implementable” without “adding to member states’ fiscal problems,” he said.

noticias.titulo: Snowden on steroids: AI agents in phones trigger surveillance fears
noticias.resumen: AI agents have already proven to be a cybersecurity risk. Now the privacy world is sounding the alarm.
noticias.texto: AI agents are lurking in your phone, hoovering up your messages, pictures and emails in a privacy breach that “makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke,” privacy proponents are warning. Privacy-preserving messaging app Signal has started blocking screenshots by default in an attempt to stop AI agents from reading people’s screens and capturing potentially sensitive data. The makers behind Signal — which is considered the industry gold standard for confidential, encrypted messaging — warned that Google, Apple and Microsoft are integrating autonomous agents “deep” within their device operating systems, allowing the agents to bypass privacy safeguards in individual apps. “The ability for billions of devices to permanently spy on their users makes the Edward Snowden revelations look like a joke,” Udbhav Tiwari, head of strategy and global affairs at Signal, told POLITICO, referring to the 2013 disclosures about mass U.S. government surveillance. Tiwari warned that governments with a penchant for surveillance could ask tech firms for access to data gathered by AI agents, skipping the need to break end-to-end encryption or install malware on someone’s device. Apple, Google and Microsoft declined to comment on Signal’s claims. Itxaso Domínguez de Olazábal, policy adviser at European digital rights group EDRi, called for “serious limits” on what AI agents can access. “There is something deeply worrying about a not-so-far-away future where the companies controlling our operating systems can effectively decide how much privacy we are allowed to have, even when we deliberately choose services designed to protect it,” she said. “Probably the most sensitive device in your entire life is your phone. If it gets nicked, the person stealing your phone is not going to have access to your whole life. We’re undoing all those safeguards by inviting AI agents onto these devices,” said Gus Hosein, executive director of privacy NGO Privacy International. Signal is pushing for makers of operating systems to provide tools so apps can opt out of AI data access and processing. Operating system level AI agents have already launched in many countries globally, but rollout is slower in the EU. Apple has cited the EU’s digital competition rulebook as a key hurdle for the rollout of its latest AI virtual assistant features. Social media giant Meta is also rolling out its own AI agent, Muse, which launched in the United Kingdom on Tuesday . Digital regulators including the Information Commissioner’s Office already warned last month that AI agent products “may amplify and accelerate risks” to consumers. The British privacy authority said this week that Meta committed to a “voluntary monitoring and reporting scheme” to enable ongoing scrutiny, and that it is preparing new guidance on how privacy law applies to AI agents. Meta has said its new AI agent is “private, safe and secure by design,” and that it has “engaged constructively” with regulators. Beyond the most high-risk situations, there are concerns AI agents could also gather data to repurpose for things like AI training or targeted advertising. Ireland’s powerful privacy regulator, which oversees data protection policies at Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft and other tech giants, is also cracking down on how “third-party” data is hoovered up by AI agents and repurposed. Third-party data pertains to someone who isn’t directly dealing with the AI agent; for example, you send a message or holiday pictures to a friend without knowing they’ve given an AI agent permission to access their messages. The Irish Data Protection Commission intervened in the past month to stop Elon Musk-owned X from feeding AI models with third party data collected by its Grok Bot, POLITICO first reported . Irish Data Protection Commissioner Niamh Sweeney said last week that it is “much more challenging” to inform third parties about their data being processed, or give them a chance to opt out, when they have “no idea” that their data could also be scooped up.

noticias.titulo: Farage suggests he could appeal to Le Pen to block Britain rejoining the EU
noticias.resumen: The Reform UK leader said with a smile: “Are you suggesting that I’d interfere in overseas politics? Quite possibly, yes.”
noticias.texto: LONDON — Nigel Farage indicated Tuesday that he might appeal to a future far-right French president in an attempt to block Britain’s reentry to the European Union. The Reform UK leader said he has been studying a rule under which France would offer the French people a referendum on allowing individual countries to join the EU after U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened a broad conversation on closer ties, not ruling out pushing to rejoin the bloc. France passed constitutional reforms in 2005 and 2008 that state its president should hold a referendum on letting any country join the EU — unless both houses of the French parliament approve the accession by a three-fifths majority. Farage suggested that Marine Le Pen, the leader of the far-right National Rally who is leading the polls ahead of next April’s presidential election, would be “pretty much as skeptical as me” about EU enlargement. Farage told a press conference in Westminster: “Whilst it’s slightly tortuous, there is still quite a strong probability that for us to join the European Union … the French would have a referendum and a right to veto over us joining. “I’ve been checking this out again. It would need to go through the assembly, etc. But there is a relatively strong possibility that there will be a referendum on it and so a lot would depend on who the French president and French prime minister were at that moment in time. “If it was to be the current bookies’ favorites of Jordan Bardella and Marine Le Pen, I don’t see them overwhelmingly endorsing the enlargement of a European project over which they’re pretty much as skeptical as me.” Asked by POLITICO if he could try to persuade a Le Pen-led France to block the U.K.’s reentry to the EU, he replied jokingly: “Are you suggesting that I’d interfere in overseas politics? Quite possibly, yes.” ‘Europe could change’ Senior figures in Burnham’s government are already aware of the French referendum rule. Burnham has also indicated publicly that his thoughts on forging closer ties with the EU may shift if the far-right gains more power in Europe. He told MPs on Monday: “Europe could change again in the next year, 18 months, and we’ll have to obviously watch how life changes.” France is not the only country that has domestic checks and balances on EU enlargement. Catherine Barnard, an academic and director of the Centre for European Legal Studies, said: “Even if all 27 member states unanimously agree to U.K. accession, further blockages may then occur at domestic level. “For example, France might need a referendum or at least three-fifths majority in both houses. Belgium would need agreement of all of its national and regional parliaments.” Burnham said Monday that it would be “unthinkable” for Britain to rejoin the EU without holding a repeat of Britain’s 2016 referendum, in which 52% voted to leave the bloc. The prime minister has previously said he would like to rejoin the EU in his lifetime, but has not yet decided whether he will put the proposition of full membership in Labour’s next election manifesto, expected by 2029. Farage said it would be “illegitimate” to rejoin the EU without a new referendum, though he batted off the suggestion that Britain might need a referendum to rejoin the single market or customs union alone. Farage also appeared to suggest there could be riots if the result of the 2016 referendum was overturned. “If people really think that voting changes nothing, they will resort to other means,” he said. “Democracy is the safety valve. Rather than setting fire to things, or smashing up buildings, or behaving even worse than that, you have a vote and you accept the result and say, ‘I’ll get the so-and-sos next time.’” Farage has not recently held a meeting with Le Pen, despite a Reform official previously suggesting that a rendezvous in Paris was being lined up by the end of October. Bardella, who is poised to be prime minister under a Le Pen presidency, unveiled an agreement with Farage in September to deport migrants who make unauthorized small boat crossings across the English Channel back to France. But the plan provoked a backlash in France , where politicians across the spectrum questioned why the country would act as a “gatekeeper” or a “subcontractor” for the U.K.

noticias.titulo: Wildberger reagiert skeptisch auf Weimers TikTok-Vorstoß
noticias.resumen: Der Digitalminister dämpft die Erwartungen an einen europäischen TikTok-Deal. Ein Verkauf allein reiche nicht – auch die Technologie dahinter müsse nach Europa kommen.
noticias.texto: BERLIN – Digitalminister Karsten Wildberger hat Zweifel an Weimers Plänen geäußert, das Europageschäft von TikTok mehrheitlich in europäische Hände zu überführen. Die Idee sei zwar grundsätzlich „sehr interessant“, sagte Wildberger am Montagabend bei einer Veranstaltung von POLITICO. Entscheidend sei aber, was Europa bei einem solchen Deal tatsächlich übernehmen könnte. Ein Kauf der Plattform allein würde aus Sicht des Ministers nicht ausreichen. Auch die zugrunde liegende Technologie müsste nach Europa übertragen werden, etwa die Technologie hinter Werbung, Datenanalyse und Nutzererfahrung. „Wenn das woanders läuft, was habe ich dann gekauft?“, sagte der Minister. „Es geht ja nicht nur um den Zugang, sondern eben auch um die technologische Fähigkeit, die dahintersteht.“ Der in Peking ansässige Mutterkonzern ByteDance müsse einem solchen Deal mit europäischen Investoren zunächst zustimmen, sagte Wildberger. Wenn klar sei, dass „beide miteinander tanzen wollen“, müsse geklärt werden, welche Teile der Plattform und ihrer Technologie tatsächlich übernommen werden könnten. Grundsätzlich schloss Wildberger eine europäische Lösung aber nicht aus. Sollte ein solcher Technologietransfer möglich sein und sich private Investoren finden, wäre das „natürlich schon eine spannende Sache“, sagte er. Weimer hatte am vergangenen Freitag in Brüssel erklärt, bereits mit europäischen Investoren über eine Mehrheitsübernahme des Europageschäfts von TikTok zu sprechen. Eine europäische Investorengruppe sei bereit, 25 bis 30 Milliarden Euro zu investieren. Deutschland und Österreich hatten den Vorstoß Anfang vergangener Woche mit Sorge über den Einfluss der Plattform auf die europäische Demokratie begründet. Wie eine solche Neuordnung durchgesetzt werden könnte, ist allerdings offen. Kritiker verweisen darauf, dass es bislang keine rechtliche Grundlage für einen erzwungenen Verkauf des TikTok-Europageschäfts gebe. Auch das Kulturstaatsministerium nennt bislang keinen konkreten Plan: „Die [gemeinsame Erklärung mit Österreich] formuliert zunächst das politische Anliegen“, teilte Weimers Haus auf Anfrage von POLITICO mit. „Dieser Unsinn entbehrt jeglicher Grundlage“, sagte ein Sprecher von TikTok gegenüber POLITICO. Die Plattform unterliege bereits umfassenden europäischen Vorschriften, darunter dem Digital Services Act (DSA) und der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) . Auch Axel Springer, der Mutterkonzern von POLITICO, soll Berichten zufolge Interesse daran haben, sich an einem möglichen Deal zu beteiligen. Ein Sprecher hatte erklärt, der Konzern sei dafür grundsätzlich offen. Auf eine Anfrage von POLITICO zu Weimers aktuellen Äußerungen reagierte der Medienkonzern zunächst nicht.

noticias.titulo: MI5 warns UK defense firms they are target of Russian attacks
noticias.resumen: An increased threat of Russian attacks across Europe has prompted British intelligence to call on U.K. defense firms to take action to protect themselves.
noticias.texto: LONDON — Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5 has warned U.K. defense firms of an increased risk of Russian attacks, such as arson, because of their support for Ukraine. British intelligence on Tuesday held a private meeting with CEOs and leading figures from the domestic defense industry to update them on the threat posed by Moscow. Following the meeting, Britain’s National Protective Security Authority (NPSA) — the protective security arm of MI5 — issued a public alert to U.K. organizations involved in assisting Ukraine’s war, warning that the Russian state is targeting them. The move comes after an uptick in sabotage attempts against European defense-related facilities this year. Britain already has protections in place for its critical national infrastructure and defense firms, including specialist policing at nuclear sites and its intelligence and counter-terrorism agencies. However, it is now asking companies to take action to protect themselves from harm. U.K. Armed Forces Minister, Louise Sandher-Jones, said in a statement after the meeting that defense firms were told to take “practical action to protect their people, technology and supply chains,” following the increased Russian threat. These steps include removing information about the company from websites and social media, including defense facilities, what weapons they make, operations and staff roles. NPSA also recommended staff at defense firms “avoid predictable routines where practicable,” making it harder for them to be targeted by Russia through its proxies or intelligence services. In September, a British man from Swindon was charged with national security offenses after he allegedly was involved in a plan, on behalf of Russia’s ⁠GRU military intelligence agency, to sabotage factories that manufacture drones.

noticias.titulo: Merz to meet Pope Leo, Meloni in Rome
noticias.resumen: The German chancellor and Pope Leo are expected to discuss human dignity, AI and Ukraine.
noticias.texto: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will meet Pope Leo XIV and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Monday, three officials familiar with the plans told POLITICO. The visit to the Vatican, Merz’s first private audience with the pope, is set to focus on human dignity, artificial intelligence and efforts to bring peace to Ukraine, two of the officials said. Merz also plans to meet Cardinal Secretary of State Pietro Parolin, the Vatican’s top diplomat, who in September used his U.N. General Assembly speech to call for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine and a path to diplomacy. A German government spokesperson declined to comment, saying the chancellor’s trips are announced on the Friday of the preceding week. Merz, a Catholic, attended Leo’s inauguration in May 2025 but did not meet the pontiff in private. Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul met Parolin at the Vatican in early October for talks that also covered AI, the war in Ukraine and Black Sea grain exports. The Vatican has mediated between Kyiv and Moscow on the return of Ukrainian children who were deported to Russia, and Leo has repeatedly offered to host direct peace talks, an offer Moscow has rejected. During a visit to France in September, the pope urged European leaders to be ready to make concessions to end the war. Leo has also made addressing the challenges posed by artificial intelligence a hallmark of his papacy. Magnifica humanitas, his first encyclical , which discusses the protection of human dignity in the age of AI, was on Merz’s summer reading list. Merz’s talks with Meloni are expected to cover the EU’s next long-term budget and the Ukraine peace talks, two of the officials said. Meloni secured Italy a seat in future negotiations as part of the European “E5” group, alongside Germany, France, the U.K. and Poland. CORRECTION: This article was updated on Nov. 24 to clarify the timings of Merz’s visit.

noticias.titulo: 7 EU countries push for ‘urgent’ visa ban on Russian and Belarusian athletes
noticias.resumen: The countries say allowing the competitors to return ”risks sending a signal of creeping acceptance of Russia’s war of aggression.”
noticias.texto: Seven European Union countries are urging governments to stop issuing visas to Russian and Belarusian athletes as international sports federations ease restrictions imposed after Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In a joint letter dated Monday , Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, Sweden’s Ulf Kristersson and Poland’s Donald Tusk, alongside the leaders of Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, warned that Russia’s sporting comeback would hand the Kremlin a victory. The European Commission proposed Monday to ban athletes competing under the Russian flag and recommended that governments consider denying them visas once the ban is approved. The proposed ban still needs the backing of all 27 EU countries. The seven leaders want governments to stop issuing visas to Russian and Belarusian athletes now, a move that could shut out even those cleared to compete under a neutral banner. They are also calling for tougher EU visa rules to restrict nonessential travel from Russia more generally. But with a legislative proposal not due until early 2027, they say the matter is “too urgent” to wait. “Allowing the Russian state to field participants in international competitions risks sending a signal of creeping acceptance of Russia’s war of aggression,” they wrote to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa. “It is simply impossible to separate sports and geopolitics.” The dispute is already playing out in winter sports. The International Ski and Snowboard Federation has cleared more than 400 athletes and support staff from Russia and Belarus to participate as neutrals this season. Poland has nevertheless ruled out granting visas to Russian ski jumpers for World Cup events in Wisła and Zakopane. Sweden has moved to exclude Russian skiers from the world championships it will host in February. Finland’s entry restrictions kept former figure skating world champions Anastasia Mishina and Aleksandr Galliamov out of last weekend’s competition in Helsinki. Russian hockey teams were also allowed back in international hockey tournaments following a decision from the Court of Arbitration for Sport on Oct. 30. But Canada, which hosts a youth competition in December, banned the Russian team from entering the country — and multiple European nations said they would not take part in the men’s senior competition next May, in Germany. Berlin has been pushing to renew the ban on Russian teams . The seven countries plan to press their case at Thursday’s EU summit in Brussels.

noticias.resumen: More than 500,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war with Ukraine, according to an estimate by a number of media organisations. The figures are based on a huge dataset that was hacked from Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat by Belarusian activist group Cyber Partisans and a Ukrainian hacker group, Silent Crow. Two independent Russian news outlets Meduza and Mediazona say the death toll may rise to more than 700,000 once missing soldiers are included.

noticias.titulo: Fico’s coalition targets postal voting by Slovaks abroad, as opposition cries foul
noticias.resumen: Slovak prime minister Robert Fico’s allies ram through a last-minute overhaul of how Slovak citizens abroad can vote. Opposition leaders accuse them of brazenly rewriting the rules to shut out hostile voters before the next election.
noticias.texto: Slovakia’s parliament voted on Tuesday (24 November) on a proposal that would abolish voting by post for its citizens living abroad in parliamentary elections, replacing it with in-person voting at Slovak embassies and consulates. In the 2023 elections, almost 59,000 citizens voted by mail, with the current opposition party emerging as the clear winner among them, receiving 62 percent of the votes. “Representatives of this coalition had no problem with postal voting for 20 years, until voters made them pay for it in the last election,” Ľudovít Ódor, Slovak MEP for Renew Europe and former prime minister, told EUobserver. “Slovaks living abroad are often critical of the current government,” Marek Hojsík, vice-president of the European Parliament and Slovak MEP, told EUobserver. “Which is precisely why this proposal raises serious questions.” “It is hard to escape the impression that the governing coalition is not concerned with election security, but rather with who will be allowed to participate in them,” he added. The proposal has become controversial not only because of its practical implications for Slovaks living abroad, but also because of the way it has been brought back onto parliament’s agenda – after already failing twice. The bill, introduced by prime minister Robert Fico’s Smer-SSD party, had already been removed from the agenda on 16 September and again on 11 November, after neither its sponsors nor the designated rapporteur attended the scheduled debates. Under parliamentary rules, the second failure should have meant that the proposal could not be discussed again for six months. “If this amendment is indeed passed, we will take the matter to the Constitutional Court,” Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová, Slovak MEP for Renew Europe, told EUobserver. Party-political motives As the organisation of elections remains primarily a national competence, EU member states retain discretion over how their citizens exercise their voting rights. For Slovak MEPs, it is interesting to see how political parties use these regulations to alter the conditions of political competition and potentially limit the ability of certain groups of citizens to have a say in the direction their country takes. “It is clear that this is a politically motivated move,” Miriam Lexmann, a Slovak MEP from the European People’s Party (EPP), told EUobserver. Read more ‘Manual for autocrats’: how Fico’s rule-of-law breaches put Slovakia in EU sanctions crosshairs It is not a new phenomena. For US president Donald Trump, mail-in ballots represent a “massive voter fraud”, he claimed. And Fico’s coalition has also echoed this argument. “Trump has claimed that the most recent US elections were manipulated because of postal voting. But there is absolutely no evidence to support these allegations,” Rasťo Kužel executive director at Memo98 , international organisation in the field of media and elections, told EUobserver. Many other EU democracies such as Germany use postal voting. For Kužel, it is a way of dividing the population. In this case, “Smer is positioning itself against people who live abroad. This is primarily about further polarising society.” This article continues, but the full version is available only to EUobserver.com subscribers. Visit account.euobserver.com/membership

noticias.titulo: Europe’s rights court clears way to return more asylum seekers to Belarus, after pressure from nine governments
noticias.resumen: On Tuesday, a ruling by the European Court of Human rights made it easier to deport able-bodied adults whenever they are being used to by hostile states like Belarus to stoke tensions. The ruling came after nine EU states complained about the Strasbourg-based court.
noticias.texto: The European Court of Human Rights has ruled EU states can return asylum seekers to Belarus when Minsk exploits them to destabilise neighbouring countries such as Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. The Tuesday (24 November) judgement spanned several separate cases involving Poland, Lithuania and Latvia at a time when Belarus was rounding up people and pushing them across its border, triggering stand-offs with authorities and a tightening of asylum rights. Read more As people die in the forests, Europe asks its human-rights court to bless pushbacks to Belarus While each case had their own individual particularities, ruling in favour of some and against others, the court now allows national authorities to return able-bodied adults to a hostile state if they are unable to prove they face an immediate danger. Small children and the disabled are exempt. The distinction is important because it only applies in the context of instrumentalisation, a catch-all phrase used to describe the orchestrated attempts by a government or state to destabilise an EU country. Some have accused Morocco of similar tactics, when over 70,000 people suddenly arrived in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in late July. Turkey has also been similarly accused previously, when thousands arrived in Greece in 2020 , laying the framework for a new EU asylum law that is supposed to respond to such scenarios. Tuesday’s verdict is likely to complicate the future efforts of those seeking asylum in Europe, as well as weigh in on 30 similar pending cases at the Strasbourg-court. It also opens the door for the European Commission to propose new policy later this year to help curb asylum whenever people are being instrumentalised in cases similar to Ceuta. Read more Poland’s pushback drive and EU asylum ‘emergency’ plan put rights ‘on a cliff edge’, warns Europe’s top rights chief Tuesday’s verdict most likely affects young males and other adults. Mattias Guyomar, the court’s president, says their removal would not violate article three of the European Convention of Human Rights, which bans torture and inhumane treatment. “Treating human beings as instruments is an affront to the values of the convention,” he said. “The reality of this phenomenon was not in doubt; it was well-documented and also publicly admitted to by Belarus,” he added, noting the court is bound to protect the integrity of the convention. noticias.titulo: MEPs are panicking about ‘Islamist entryism’ while the real infiltrators are the far-right and their foreign backers
noticias.resumen: Various investigations and reports now point to how foreign entities are engaged in an industrialisation and weaponisation of Islamophobia across Europe and how European Muslim citizens and organisations have become collateral damage in wider geopolitical and ideological battles.
noticias.texto: Not long after US president George W. Bush launched his discredited “War on Terror” following the terrible 9/11 attacks, well-meaning friends often asked why I did not change my surname. It wouldn’t be a bureaucratic hassle since I was married (at the time) to a Spaniard and a more European surname would, if nothing else, make it easier to travel, book restaurants and live a normal life at a time of surging Islamophobia. Someone else suggested that instead of time trying to build bridges between people and cultures, I should become a professional Islam-basher like Aayan Hirsi Ali . It would be much more financially rewarding. Or why didn’t I just tell people I was a Buddhist? I could then just get on with my life, without all the questions, insults and innuendos. I did not follow up on any of the “friendly” suggestions – or the other not-so friendly ones which told me to go “back home”. noticias.titulo: EU mining plans in the Western Balkans face local resistance
noticias.resumen: While EU leaders hunt for “green” metals in the Western Balkans, villagers from Jadar to Vareš warn the only thing guaranteed so far is polluted land, opaque permits and profits vanishing far from their communities.
noticias.texto: “We have achieved something that rarely happens when multinational companies are involved: we stopped a mining project before it could be implemented”, says Nebojša Petković, an activist from Ne damo Jadar (We Won’t Give Up Jadar) group, a collective against lithium mining in the valley of Jadar in western Serbia. “Usually, citizens rise up in large numbers only once a mine starts causing damage, but by then it is too late.” The price they have paid for this is unprecedented persecution by the authorities: people have been fired, arrested, threatened, and subjected to media demonisation. The Jadar project, run by the British-Australian Rio Tinto company, is listed as one of the strategic projects under the European Union’s Critical Raw Materials Act of June 2025. The European Commission also signed a strategic partnership with Serbia on sustainable raw materials, battery value chains, and electric vehicles on 19 July 2025. Read more From protest to power: Serbia’s student movement prepares to dismantle Vučić’s regime And protests that had already started earlier against the lithium mining in a countryside where people live from agriculture, exploded that summer. “I think this anger, especially when it comes to the lithium mine in Serbia, but also a little bit in Bosnia, it’s also going towards the EU because it feels that the EU is also playing its part in it,” said Frauke Seebass, a researcher from Hellenic Foundation for European & Foreign Policy (ELIAMEP) in Athens. EU plans for green transition and development of renewable energy technologies, such as wind turbines, batteries, and solar panels require critical raw materials such as lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper and rare earth elements, strategic documents show. The reserves in the Western Balkan countries seem to be a good solution for the EU to be able to respond to those needs, but they face huge local resistance, especially in Serbia. Citizens fear that the land where they live and work will be destroyed, as they already saw in some of Rio Tinto’s exploratory actions. Although this has become an illustrative example of a persistent battle against mining in populated areas, the Western Balkans region is facing more of these hot spots. This region suffers from lack of transparency, as local communities are often excluded from decisions that will affect their land, water, and livelihoods, lack of democracy and rule of law, especially when it comes to environmental standards – a reality that challenges EU plans and needs when it comes to mining projects, as a series of reports published by the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung (FES) in Berlin also highlights. The low governance score in Serbia was also noted in the European Court of Auditors special report on critical raw materials mining. Read more EU seeks closer embrace of Western Balkans leaders ‘People are just really fed up with not being asked’ ELIAMEP’s Seebass explained that the majority of the problems lay in the legislative and governance levels: “Even if you have legislation in place, it is often not implemented, and there is a lack of political will to implement these kinds of legislation, especially those for protecting the environment.” Although she thinks that it can be an opportunity if it is taken seriously, with qualified people, high environmental standards and using the secondary raw materials, she admits that at the moment it is not. “In examples such as the mine in Bor in Serbia, but also, for example, the chromium mining in Albania, you see that there is very little positive effect for the local population, since the costs are actually higher to the local population than the money that they make – and this is clearly a governance issue,” she said. “In Bosnia and Herzegovina, we see that local authorities are often the ones that are more interested in making money than to protect the people. About an hour from Sarajevo in Vares, there is an ongoing mining project and people are trying to get access to information on pollution levels, but they face a lot of opposition from the local authorities, including local council people, but also the companies themselves”, she added. And while the protests in Serbia blew up to a massive scale, she found worrying that in Bosnia and Herzegovina some actors were exploiting existing ethnic and religious divisions in the region, deliberately fuelling tensions between communities to prevent them from uniting in opposition to mining projects. “People are just really fed up with not being asked”, Seebass said, adding: “We also see that there’s a lot of interest on the side of some governments to bring in money no matter what.” And that’s why Petković from Ne damo Jadar described the Jadar project as “a representative example of the collusion between a corrupt government, the corrupt capital of multinational corporations, and criminals.” Read more Green groups file complaint over EU water protection review, citing mining lobbying What now? The Jadar project is currently on hold, Petković explained. “The boreholes have been closed and rehabilitated, and the company says the project is in a care and maintenance phase. In general, the company has done nothing on the ground for more than five years that would advance the project, all it has done is maintain the boreholes, which it closed this year”, he said. But despite saying that “strategic projects must also meet public acceptance obligations and demonstrate engagement with the local population”, the EU is sticking to its plans. “The Commission remains in contact with Rio Tinto to monitor the Jadar project”, a commission spokesperson wrote in a response to the Friedrich Ebert Foundation. “Both parties are working toward the implementation of the partnership”, they said. Parliamentary elections in Serbia on 25 October ended the 14-year rule of the Serbian Progressive Party led by Aleksandar Vučić. The Students’ List , a grassroots anti-corruption movement, won with absolute majority. The list is full of academics, professors, experts, and other prominent individuals from different fields, including agricultural activist Zlatko Kokanović from Ne damo Jadar. Petković expects the new government to review every aspect of the mining project, to establish what was illegal in the way it was carried out, assess the damage caused by the exploration activities, trace the flow of money, and prosecute everyone responsible for pollution and fraud. “I expect Rio Tinto to pack up and leave Serbia, and the EU to stop insisting that the Jadar project go ahead and stop using it as leverage against the new government”, he said, referring to concern that Serbia’s accession to the EU now also depends on the development of the mine.

noticias.titulo: El Gobierno incrementa las deducciones de IRPF para los autónomos, que solo tendrán que hacer una declaración de IVA al año
noticias.texto:
El Gobierno incrementa las deducciones de IRPF para los autónomos, que solo tendrán que hacer una declaración de IVA al año
- 2,6 millones de autónomos se beneficiarán de una rebaja del 10% en el IRPF
- Los que facturen menos de 85.000 euros anuales ya no tendrán que hacer declaraciones trimestrales de IVA
El Consejo de Ministros celebrado este martes ha aprobado un paquete de medidas fiscales enfocado en aliviar la carga tributaria y administrativa de los trabajadores autónomos. Para poner en marcha estas medidas, el Gobierno ha tenido en cuenta "el crecimiento de costes" que afrontan los trabajadores por cuenta propia. El Ejecutivo y pretende, además, simplificar las obligaciones tributarias para los autónomos a través de "fórmulas para planificar mejor el ejercicio 2027" en palabras del ministro de Hacienda, Arcadi España.
Aunque el texto completo y los detalles técnicos quedarán fijados tras su publicación en el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE), las líneas principales de este paquete fiscal establecen una rebaja del IRPF de los autónomos que les ahorrará 465 millones de euros y la puesta en marcha de un régimen especial de IVA para aquellos que facturen menos de 85.000 euros.
Más deducciones en la Renta
España, ha explicado en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo que el real decreto ley aprobado incrementa del 5% al 10% la deducción por provisiones y gastos de difícil justificación, al tiempo que amplía el límite máximo de la deducción de 2.000 a 3.000 euros, con efecto en el ejercicio 2026.
Por su parte, quienes tributan por el sistema de módulos verán ampliada del 5% al 10% la reducción general sobre su rendimiento neto correspondiente a 2026.
Para las actividades agrícolas, ganaderas y forestales, esa reducción general sube del 10% previsto inicialmente al 15%, manteniéndose además las minoraciones extraordinarias del 35% por adquisición de gasóleo agrícola y del 15% por compra de fertilizantes.
Estas dos medidas beneficiarán en conjunto a 2,6 millones de trabajadores autónomos en toda España, según las cifras oficiales presentadas por el Ministerio de Hacienda (1,6 millones en estimación directa y un millón en módulos).
Adiós al Modelo 130
Con el objetivo de simplificar las obligaciones en el IRPF, los autónomos en estimación directa, aquellos que pagan impuestos por el beneficio real de su negocio, calculado restando sus gastos deducibles a sus ingresos reales, que facturen menos de 85.000 euros anuales dejarán de estar obligados a presentar los pagos fraccionados trimestrales (Modelo 130), siempre que la cuota diferencial de su última declaración haya sido negativa o superior a los pagos fraccionados realizados.
"Pasamos de cuatro declaraciones a una, con el ahorro que significa en la complejidad administrativa, burocrática y de la carga de sus obligaciones tributarias" ha asegurado el ministro de Hacienda en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Ministros. España ha explicado que "solo habrá que hacer un pago a cuenta en abril, julio y octubre cuyo cálculo realizará la Agencia Tributaria y se basará en dividir por cuatro la cuota del ejercicio anterior". Se trata de un régimen voluntario que afectará a 1,1 millón de autónomos en España.
En el caso de los profesionales en estimación directa que superen los 85.000 euros de facturación anual y mantengan la obligación de presentar el pago fraccionado, el tipo aplicable se rebaja del 20% al 19%.
El presidente de la Federación Nacional de Asociaciones de Trabajadores Autónomos (ATA), Lorenzo Amor, ha asegurado que llevaban "tres años solicitando esa medida" y ha criticado que se apruebe "a cinco días de las elecciones".
El Consejo de Ministros de este martes también ha acordado volver a retrasar la entrada en vigor de Verifactu, el nuevo sistema de facturación verificable en sistemas informáticos para empresas y autónomos. Su puesta en marcha se pospone hasta octubre del 2028, y coincidirá con el inicio de la obligatoriedad de la facturación electrónica para autónomos tal y como ha explicado el ministro España.

noticias.titulo: Bruselas amenaza a España con abrir un expediente por la deuda y el desvío de gasto
noticias.texto:
Bruselas amenaza a España con abrir un expediente por la deuda y el desvío de gasto
- Insta al país a adoptar medidas presupuestarias para no incumplir las reglas fiscales en 2026 y 2027
- Calcula que España cerrará este año con un desvío de 5.100 millones este año y 12.000 millones el que viene
La Comisión Europea ha advertido este martes de que España corre el riesgo de incumplir "de forma sustancial" las recomendaciones fiscales para 2026 y 2027 y le pide adoptar medidas para ajustar su política presupuestaria. De no hacerlo, la Comisión ha amenazado al país con abrir un procedimiento por déficit excesivo en primavera del próximo año por el exceso de deuda y el desvío de gasto.
"Si se confirma, basándose en los datos oficiales en primavera del año próximo, la Comisión Europea preparará un informe bajo el artículo 126.3 del Tratado evaluando el cumplimiento con el criterio de deuda. Esto podría llevar a la apertura de un procedimiento por déficit excesivo", ha señalado el comisario europeo de Economía, Valdis Dombrovskis, en una comparecencia antes de presentar los informes del llamado Semestre Europeo en una rueda de prensa.
Dicho artículo establece que, si un Estado miembro no cumple con las recomendaciones del Consejo para reducir un déficit excesivo, este último puede formular una advertencia al Estado en cuestión para que adopte las medidas necesarias en un plazo determinado. El Consejo puede también, por mayoría cualificada, suspender determinados derechos derivados de la aplicación de los Tratados al Estado miembro de que se trate, incluyendo los derechos de voto en el Consejo.
Además de España, otros siete están en riesgo de incumplir las reglas fiscales el próximo año: Eslovenia, Países Bajos, Lituania, Luxemburgo y Malta, así como Alemania y República Checa, aunque estos dos últimos no sobrepasarían los umbrales que podrían dar lugar a un expediente.
De ellos, tan solo España y Eslovenia tienen riesgo de incumplir las reglas fiscales este mismo año. Si así se confirma, tras su revisión en primavera, la Comisión elaborará un informe que puede dar lugar a incoar un procedimiento de déficit excesivo. Para evitarlo, ha dicho Dombrovskis, ambos países deberán adoptar las medidas adecuadas en los presupuestos de 2027.
Un desvío de 5.100 millones este año
Bruselas calcula que España cerrará este año con un desvío de la senda fiscal acumulado desde 2024 equivalente al 0,9% del PIB, por encima del límite del 0,6% que contemplan las reglas presupuestarias. La diferencia de tres décimas equivale, en términos absolutos, a unos 5.100 millones de euros.
El desvío es mayor que el desfase del 0,45% que Bruselas anticipó en mayo y la institución atribuye el incremento de los últimos meses principalmente en los paquetes de ayudas adoptados desde entonces por la crisis en Oriente Medio, pero también al mayor gasto público derivado del aumento de las plantillas de empleados públicos en las comunidades autónomas.
En el caso del próximo año, el desvío asciende hasta los 12.000 millones, sin tener en cuenta el impacto de las aprobadas en los últimos Consejos de Ministros.
Cabe recordar que España suma tres ejercicios sin presentar cuentas públicas. Los últimos se aprobaron en 2023 y, desde entonces, se han prorrogado en 2024, 2025, 2026 y, previsiblemente, se harán también durante los primeros meses de 2027 ante la falta de acuerdo entre el Gobierno y el resto de partidos.
En el marco de la Unión Europea, también Bélgica y Letonia aún tienen pendiente presentar sus presupuestos para el próximo ejercicio.
Evolución de los procedimientos de déficit excesivo
En el caso de los diez procedimientos de déficit excesivos abiertos actualmente, en ocho países —Austria, Bélgica, Finlandia, Francia, Italia, Polonia, Rumanía y Eslovaquia—, se mantiene en suspenso. Esto significa que no se adoptan nuevas medidas en el procedimiento en esta fase, pero que permanece abierto y los Estados miembros siguen sujetos a la correspondiente recomendación del Consejo. La Comisión volverá a evaluar la situación la próxima primavera, cuando estén disponibles los datos de ejecución de 2026.
En el caso de Italia, el Ejecutivo comunitario espera que el país corrija su déficit excesivo en 2026 y que se mantenga por debajo del 3% en 2027 y 2028, teniendo en cuenta la flexibilidad proporcionada por la cláusula de escape nacional para la defensa y la seguridad energética. En vista de ello, la Comisión podría considerar su derogación en la primavera de 2027, han avanzado.
Mientras que, para Bulgaria y Hungría, la Comisión considera que ambos países tienen un riesgo de no cumplimiento "grave", lo que justifica avanzar a una fase más estricta del procedimiento. Por tanto, la Comisión recomienda al Consejo que adopte una decisión con arreglo al artículo 126, apartado 8, del Tratado de Funcionamiento de la UE que constate la ausencia de medidas efectivas.

El voto exterior y el postdebate a ocho centran la campaña mientras los candidatos apuran los plazos con varias entrevistas
- 										
													Día 1: Arranque de campaña Los partidos dan el pistoletazo de salida en la carrera hacia el 29-NDía 2: Nuevos formatos digitales Los candidatos inauguran la campaña atreviéndose con grandes mítines y nuevos formatos digitalesDía 3: Primer sábado de campaña Primer sábado de campaña con reproches cruzados entre los candidatosDía 4: Primer domingo de campaña Los partidos culminan el primer fin de semana de campaña ofreciendo sus recetas para el 29NDía 5: Cuarto día de campaña Las propuestas fiscales o sobre migración, en el foco en una jornada de campaña con nuevos cruces de reprochesDía 6: Inmigración irregular, en campaña La inmigración irregular, IVA progresivo en los suministros, propuestas laborales y de vivienda, en campañaDía 7: Sin mítines de Sánchez, Feijóo y Abascal Sin mitines de Sánchez, Feijóo y Abascal, unas palabras polémicas de Ayuso se cuelan en la campañaDía 8: Cara a cara entre Sánchez y Feijóo El cara a cara entre Sánchez y Feijóo y unas declaraciones de Puigdemont marcan la jornadaDía 9: El ecuador de la campaña La resaca del cara a cara Sánchez-Feijóo marca el ecuador de la campaña Horas después del debate a ocho en RTVE, que sirvió para evidenciar la confrontación entre dos los dos bloques ideológicos de la izquierda y la derecha, continúa la campaña electoral para los candidatos, que aprovechan las últimas horas para sumar votos a su papeleta multiplicando su presencia en medios de comunicación y mitines. Este martes Pedro Sánchez ha ofrecido una entrevista en Radio Nacional y por la tarde multiplicará su presencia con actos en Huesca y Barcelona. Alberto Núñez Feijóo también ha sido entrevistado en la radio, en su caso Onda Cero, y por la tarde se trasladará a Alicante. Santiago Abascal, de Vox, ha declinado la entrevista electoral en RTVE y ha reducido su agenda, mientras la candidata de Frente Amplio, Ada Colau, ha ofrecido por la mañana entrevistas en Antena 3 y el podcast Carne Cruda y por la noche se enfrentará en un Cara a Cara con el popular Xabier García Albiol, con quien podrá confrontar los programas de vivienda de ambas formaciones. Feijóo siembra dudas sobre la limpieza electoral y el PP, de nuevo, abucheado en el País Vasco El candidato del PP a la Presidencia del Gobierno, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ha puesto en duda la limpieza del sistema electoral por las "urnas de cartón" en los consulados para que voten ciudadanos a los que se les otorgó la nacionalidad por la llamada 'ley de nietos' y ha recordado "los antecedentes" de "modificación de sus primarias". "El señor Sánchez y la limpieza electoral son dos conceptos bastante contradictorios", ha asegurado en declaraciones en Onda Cero. No obstante, ha mostrado su confianza y fe en que los cónsules de nuestro país "blinden los votos que se emiten en las urnas de los consulados" y de que "esas urnas de cartón" que no sabe para qué se ponen, ha afirmado, estén "bien supervisadas". En un mitin en Andoain (Guipúzcoa), un grupo de radicales ha increpado y abucheado a la portavoz del PP en el Congreso, Ester Muñoz, y al cabeza de lista por esta provincia, Jon Echeverría, a los que han gritado 'Kanpora' (Fuera), 'Alde hemendik' (Marcharos de aquí) e insultos como fascista. Muñoz ha acusado de la "agresividad" a Bildu y ha recordado que en el debate a ocho preguntó al portavoz de la formación 'abertzale' si pensaba mandar a sus "cachorros". "Al parecer les han dicho que no nos agredan físicamente, pero sí verbalmente. Y aquí están los cachorros de Bildu", ha señalado Muñoz. Echeverría, por su parte, ha dicho que "ellos son los fascistas": "Quién se creen para decirnos que nos vayamos de aquí", ha reprochado. El secretario general del PP, Miguel Tellado, ha hecho campaña en Leganés (Madrid), donde ha criticado que el Gobierno sea "tibio" condenando estos actos de violencia. Además, ha cargado contra Pedro Sánchez y el PSOE, al que ha llamado "mafia". Por ello, ha apelado a "arrasarle en las urnas" para que "tenga que abandonar la política". "Tenemos que sacar ese veneno de la política española", ha insistido. En un desayuno informativo, el cabeza de lista del PP al Congreso por Barcelona, Xavier García Albiol, ha asegurado que el expresidente de la Generalitat Carles Puigdemont está "políticamente amortizado" y no cree que su amnistía pueda influir en el 29N. Se ha pronunciado así después de la decisión del Tribunal Supremo de aplicar la amnistía al líder de Junts. Sánchez advierte: "PP y Vox, si no suman, no van a aceptar el resultado" El presidente del Gobierno y candidato del PSOE a la reelección, Pedro Sánchez, ha arrancado el último martes de campaña con una entrevista en RNE. En ella, ha pedido una movilización "contundente" el próximo 29 de noviembre y ha advertido que si "PP y Vox, si no suman, no van a aceptar el resultado". Sánchez ha criticado algunos comentarios de dirigentes del PP que, según él, han puesto en duda un sistema electoral "garantista y reconocido internacionalmente". Sánchez también ha también ha replicado en la entrevista a Radio Nacional al expresidente Felipe González que con el "voto en blanco no se frena a la ultraderecha", después de que el exmandatario haya dicho que no votará al PSOE en estas elecciones. "Con el blanco no se frena a la ultraderecha. Se frena con el rojo", ha insistido. Asimismo, el presidente y candidato socialista a la reelección ha vuelto a defender la "limpieza" de su administración y del PSOE. "No hay financiación irregular", ha dicho, en referencia a su partido. Asimismo, ha dicho que siempre "han dado" toda la documentación que se les ha requerido. En el marco de la campaña electoral, Sánchez celebrará este miércoles por la tarde dos mítines. El primero será a partir de las 16 horas en Huesca y el segundo será en Barcelona, a partir de las 19 horas. En el caso de este último, el PSOE ha tenido que buscar un nuevo recinto para poder albergar a toda la gente que se prevé que asista. Finalmente, el espacio elegido ha sido uno de los pabellones de la Fira de Barcelona en Montjuïc. Abascal declina participar el programa La Hora de la 1, donde la Junta Electoral le asignó 20 minutos Dentro del espacio que la Junta Electoral Central asigna a los distintos partidos políticos, el candidato de Vox Santiago Abascal estaba invitado este martes a participar en el programa La hora de la 1, para ser entrevistado por la periodista Silvia Intxaurrondo. El líder de Vox, al que le correspondían hoy 20 minutos según lo marcado por el órgano electoral, no ha asistido a la cita y la entrevista no se ha podido llevar a cabo. Además, ha despejado su agenda y no tiene actos ni miércoles ni jueves. Precisamente la Junta Electoral Central ha abierto expediente a Intxaurrondo por una posible vulneración de la neutralidad, ya que, tras la entrevista de Santiago Abascal en el programa La Revuelta de RTVE, la presentadora del programa matinal reflexionó si la televisión pública debería dar cabida a la "extrema derecha" y se preguntaba "¿Dónde acaba el pluralismo y empieza la normalización de los discursos discriminatorios?". Este martes, Intxaurrondo ha dicho que recibe la sanción "con orgullo" y ha anunciado que acudirá a los tribunales para revertir "un ataque a la libertad de prensa". "Creo que es la primera vez que la Junta Electoral Central abre un expediente sancionador contra una periodista a título personal por hacer preguntas y plantear un debate", ha trasladado Intxaurrondo. Quién si ha tenido agenda ha sido la portavoz parlamentaria de Vox, Pepa Millán, que ha hecho a la movilización en las urnas en favor de su partido el próximo domingo "para poder superar todas las trampas y los obstáculos que el PSOE seguramente ya tenga preparadas para estas elecciones". Colau reivindica las medidas de sumar del Ejecutivo de las que presume Sánchez: "Hay que votar al original, no a la copia" La candidata de Frente Amplio a la presidencia del Gobierno, Ada Colau, ha reivindicado una vez más las medidas del Ejecutivo de Coalición de las que, ha asegurado, presume Pedro Sánchez en campaña: "Parece que vamos anunciando medidas nuevas y a los pocos días las incorpora el PSOE". Precisamente este martes la formación ha dado a conocer una campaña titulada "Que no sea la última vez". Con un vídeo acompañado por la canción "Don’t stop me now", de Queen, celebran logros como la Reforma Laboral, la subida del SMI y las pensiones, La Ley Riders o los avances en dependencia, conseguidos por los ministerios del espacio político de la formación. “Este 29N, nos jugamos que no sea la última. Este 29N, vota Frente Amplio. https://t.co/1V3cwzTZsn“ — Frente Amplio (@Frente_Amplio_) November 24, 2026 Frente a esa estrategia de Sánchez "que parece que en campaña se anima mucho y se pone progresista", Colau ha insistido en que lo importante es "que lo que decimos en campaña se pueda trasladar al BOE". Y para que eso suceda, ha asegurado, "hay que votar al original y no a la copia, y ese es Frente Amplio". Colau se ha referido también al manifiesto que este lunes firmaron unas doscientas personalidades del mundo de la cultura para apoyar su formación política y ha vuelto a reivindicar que el voto a Frente Amplio es doblemente útil: "No me extraña que la cultura se movilice para conseguir ese voto valiente que planta cara a la extrema derecha y consigue ampliar derechos", porque "allí donde gobiernan están aplicando la censura en la cultura". ERC pide subirlas pensiones según el IPC de Cataluña y blindarlo en la Constitución El líder de ERC, Oriol Junqueras, ha pedido este martes que las pensiones suban según el índice de precios al consumo (IPC) de cada comunidad autónoma, lo que supondría que en Cataluña aumentaran, y que la revalorización esté blindada en la Constitución. En declaraciones a los periodistas tras reunirse con el secretario general de UGT de Cataluña, Camil Ros, en la sede del sindicato, Junqueras ha afirmado que Esquerra está "ferozmente y salvajemente comprometida en la defensa de las pensiones" y ha sostenido que el PP, Vox y Aliança Catalana suponen un riesgo. "Los salarios y las pensiones tienen que responder al coste de la vida. Defendemos un salario mínimo en Cataluña y defendemos unas pensiones mínimas en Cataluña", ha señalado Junqueras. Por otro lado, ha lanzado dardos al PSOE y a Frente Amplio por el paquete de medidas sociales con nuevos permisos aprobados este martes por el Gobierno. "Han tenido ocho años para hacerlo y lo han aprobado tres días antes de las elecciones. Es la mejor demostración de que votar al PSOE y al Frente Amplio y Comuns es perder el tiempo y de por qué hay que votar a ERC, ha indicado. Al respecto, ha afirmado que "si Esquerra Republicana no aprieta, empuja y obliga, aquí nadie se mueve; en particular ni el PSOE ni el Frente Amplio". Nogueras: “En 2023 dijimos no a un Gobierno de PP y Vox. Lo mantenemos” La candidata de Junts, Miriam Nogueras, ha descartado esta mañana facilitar un gobierno de PP y Junts con los escaños del Congreso que las urnas les otorguen el próximo 29N. “En 2023 ya dijimos que no a un Gobierno de PP y Vox. Lo mantenemos aquí”, ha dicho Nogueras, que ha explicado que no darán sus votos “a los que están diciendo que prohibirán nuestra lengua, se cargarán nuestras instituciones, nuestra historia y nuestra identidad”. El escenario que manejan los de Junts es que su formación, tras las elecciones “sea decisiva”, con el objetivo de “detener a la derecha y la extrema derecha y frenar la decadencia de las políticas de un PSOE arrastrado por Podemos” y por las de Colau. La de Junts se ha referido además a las medidas sociales adoptadas por el Consejo de Ministros, para decir que “me chirría un poco lo que está haciendo el Gobierno estos últimos días de campaña”: “Utiliza herramientas que se pueden cuestionar, aprobando medidas sin mayoría para ello. Y les está sirviendo para tapar la victoria del independentismo ”, en referencia a la decisión del Supremo de aplicar la amnistía a Carles Puigdemont. Aitor Esteban defiende que "la inmensa mayoría de los partidos, menos el PNV, está metida en bloques" El presidente del PNV, Aitor Esteban, ha destacado la actitud de Maribel Vaquero en el debate a ocho de los portavoces parlamentarios en RTVE, aislándose del "ruido de Madrid", y ha lamentado que "la inmensa mayoría" de las formaciones políticas, a excepción de su partido, está "metida en bloques". En una entrevista en Radio Nervión, Esteban se ha mostrado confiado en que, en las elecciones generales del próximo domingo, el PNV logrará revalidar sus 5 escaños y, por tanto, podrá formar grupo parlamentario propio.Tras vaticinar que "probablemente va a haber un cambio de Gobierno" como resultado de los comicios, ha advertido de que "tiene que haber un Grupo Vasco fuerte que haya conocido diferentes circunstancias" y "capaz de aprovechar todos los momentos". EH Bildu pide un voto "masivo" como "garantía" para derrotar al "bloque reaccionario" El candidato de EH Bildu al Congreso de los Diputados por Álava, Mikel Otero, ha hecho un llamamiento a la ciudadanía a "votar masivamente" a la coalición como "garantía" y "voto seguro" para derrotar al "bloque reaccionario". Otero, en un acto político celebrado en Legutio (Álava), ha afirmado que "solo con EH Bildu será posible conformar una mayoría progresista". Para lograrlo, el candidato ha invitado a la ciudadanía a formar parte de "la ola de ilusión" que representa EH Bildu. "Desde hoy hasta el viernes, tenemos que organizar la inteligencia colectiva de este pueblo para que la emoción, la sonrisa y la esperanza lleguen a todas las calles, puestos de trabajo y grupos de WhatsApp de Euskal Herria", ha manifestado. Montero pide ampliar los permisos a "la familia elegida" e ironiza: "Que vivamos siempre en campaña" La cabeza de lista de Podemos a las elecciones generales, Irene Montero, ha reconocido en una entrevista en Cadena Ser que su partido ha cometido algunos errores en los últimos años, principalmente por cuestiones internas, pero ha considerado que han perdido más votos por sus "aciertos políticos", como los "avances feministas contundentes". Después, en referencia a la ampliación de los permisos retribuidos que este martes aprueba el Ejecutivo, ha pedido ampliarlos a la "familia elegida" y ha ironizado que querría que "vivamos siempre en campaña": porque "aparecen permisos retribuidos y derechos". Coalición Canaria condiciona su voto a la investidura a un compromiso de inversión de 2.000 millones en las islas La candidata de Coalición Canaria, Cristina Valido, ha anunciado que su eventual apoyo a la investidura del candidato que aspire a presidir el Gobierno tras las elecciones de este domingo queda condicionado a diez compromisos que implican 2.084 millones de euros de inversión las islas. Además, Valido ha señalado que tienen "muy buenas sensaciones" de cara al 29N porque los únicos sondeos a los que les hacen caso son "los de la calle" y no aquellos con apenas 30 consultas en Canarias o los encargados "por una parte interesada". Pontón reclama "menos bombas y más vivienda" y concentrar en el BNG el voto pacifista La portavoz nacional del BNG, Ana Pontón, ha pedido este concentrar en el BNG el voto pacifista de quienes defienden que haya "menos bombas y más vivienda", aumentando el gasto social y reduciendo el militar. "Menos tanques y más vivienda, menos armas y más médicos, menos bombas y más atención a la dependencia", ha reivindicado Pontón en un acto electoral celebrado en Pontevedra junto a la candidata al Congreso, Carme da Silva. UPN apuesta por poner la educación "en el centro de prioridades" La candidata de UPN-PP al Senado Maribel García Malo ha asegurado que ha llegado "el momento de volver a poner la educación en el centro de las prioridades", y ha añadido que se necesita "más apoyo" para los alumnos que tienen dificultades y "más libertad" para que las familias puedan elegir el modelo educativo que desean. "Desde la coalición UPN-Partido Popular creemos que ha llegado el momento de volver a poner la educación en el centro de las prioridades. Necesitamos recuperar la cultura del esfuerzo, necesitamos más apoyo para los alumnos que tienen dificultades y necesitamos más libertad para que las familias puedan elegir el modelo educativo que quieren para sus hijos", ha declarado.
